newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.20/1.15 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.17/1.12 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.73/1.68 percent against 1.70/1.65 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$98.65/98.70.
September 2001 ended at S$97.40/97.45 versus Monday's S$97.47/97.52 and June 2003 at S$95.40/95.45 against S$95.47/95.52.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 1-1/2 1-3/8 percent from 1-5/8 1-1/2 percent.
